state:
Goal `core-test-1-2`, stage 2. `Core\Test::advance`, `answerHttp`, `answerSocket`,
`assertCalled`, `assertNeverCalled`, `assertEquals` and `assertEqualsDeep` have every proof:
`about.md`, three examples, one attack, a bench, and a Rust `covers:` test in
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs`'s tests module.

The `assertEqualsDeep` attack found a hang: a graph of shared nodes was walked once per path.
The walk now keeps `Proven`, the pairs of objects already found equal, and
`tests/conformance/core/test-assert-equals-deep-walks-a-shared-node-once.nvst` pins it.

The five members still owed are `assertCount`, `assertContains`, `assertMatchesInline`,
`assertDoesNotThrow` and `assertCompletes`. Each owes examples, hostile, perf and tests
(`bun nv proofs --owed --only ...`). They run at the top level of a program under `nvs run`,
with no `#[Test]` class; `bun nv try <files>` runs them that way. A bench needs
`bun nv proofs --record-perf --only '<member>'`. Any edit to `test.rs` makes every
`Core\Test` bench figure stale, so a slice that changes Rust there re-records all of them. A keyed array is declared `array<int>`, never
`array<string, int>`; there is no `intdiv` and no `!==`.

A Rust test of a failing assertion reads its sentence with `ctx.take_pending()`.
`assert_equals_and_assert_equals_deep_agree_below_the_object_row` is the shape for a member
taking plain values: an `asserted(ctx, member, actual, expected)` helper over
`nvs_runtime::call`, passing `Value::null()` for the omitted `message`.
